questions.q: Which table stores group records in ServiceNow?
options: sys_user_role
sys_user_grmember
sys_user_group
sys_user_has_role
questions.explain: sys_user_group is the single source of truth for teams, just as sys_user is for individual people.

questions.q: What is sys_user_grmember, and why does it matter even though the UI never makes you open it directly?
options: A deprecated table no longer used by ServiceNow
A duplicate of sys_user_group with no real purpose
A table that only tracks group managers, not members
The many-to-many join table behind group membership — you need to know it exists to write reports or scripts that query membership programmatically
questions.explain: The Group Members and Groups related lists on both forms are just two views into rows on sys_user_grmember, which has user and group reference fields.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between an incident's Assignment group field and its Assigned to field?
options: They are two names for the same field
Assigned to is required and Assignment group is never used
Assignment group only applies to change requests, not incidents
Assignment group routes work to a team's visible queue (sys_user_group); Assigned to optionally narrows it to one specific person (sys_user)
questions.explain: This two-level structure keeps work visible to a whole team before (or even without) one person claiming it individually.

questions.q: What is the Group Email field used for?
options: It stores the login email of the group's first member
It's a shared mailbox address notifications use when a message targets the whole assignment group, not one person
It is only visible to the admin role
It replaces the need for a Manager field
questions.explain: When a notification targets the Assignment group, Group Email ensures the whole team sees the alert rather than relying on one member to forward it.

questions.q: A new admin assigns every incoming incident directly to a named person instead of an assignment group first. What's a real consequence of skipping assignment groups?
options: SLA and escalation logic stops working for every record in the system
Nothing changes — Assignment group has no practical effect
Incidents become impossible to close
Work can get stuck with one person who's unavailable, and managers lose easy visibility into team-wide workload
questions.explain: Assignment groups keep work visible to the whole team and are what SLA/escalation logic is typically written against — skipping them throws away that visibility.
